scope: Bounded source and historical terminal review on CPU3. No model imports, codec execution, live scientific-output inspection or corpus reads.

findings.finding: The general previous/current word information source is already modeled, but exact standalone suffix8/suffix2/field equivalence is not established.
findings.details: words_[1] accumulates current WRT-class word hash; delimiter shifts into words_[2..6] even on repeated delimiters. AddWord nonstationary keys include {1,2}, {1,3}, {2,3}, {1,2,4}; match keys include {1,2,3} and {7,2}. words_[0] is a persistent masked hash, not an exact case-preserving current suffix.

findings.finding: The internal FXCM has stronger completed-word state than the outer manager alone suggests.
findings.details: procWord reconstructs dictionary spelling into setbuf/setbufstem. Stemmed sentence, paragraph and stream histories feed current-plus-prior word contexts. Bracket, first-character, paragraph, nowiki/math/pre state conditions several contexts. These are neither exact ASCII suffix tuples nor the standalone seven-field opcode rule.

findings.finding: Direct key transfer crosses frontend, prediction and update coordinates.
findings.details: Standalone history tracks ASCII letters in opcode-modeled bytes, preserving case and updating even copied bytes. XML opcode bytes hide tag spellings and change delimiter boundaries. FX2 predicts stored WRT bits, with dictionary code bytes, capitalization controls, escapes and byte remapping; a completed stored event may release multiple raw letters. Raw letters may affect future predictions only after their complete stored event is observed. FXCM's partial dictionary index is a different causal state, not permission to reveal actual future spelling. Native dictionary pretraining must remain unchanged and separate from a new document observer.

findings.finding: Generic raw-history rebirth is not justified by old TWINSTREAM gain.
findings.details: Old raw-only observation saved5808 bytes on a different parent; shared raw/WRT variants lost6498/6453 and capacity control2478. decision: Do not treat standalone previous-word gain as a missing-information diagnosis for FX2; no native predictor gate selected.
smallest_follow_up_question: Can a synthetic, decoder-causal WRT event-boundary witness identify a concrete exact case-preserving previous-suffix8/current-suffix2/field distinction that the active native word keys merge, without revealing a pending dictionary codeword? Use fixed dictionary-completion, capitalization, repeated-delimiter and escaped-byte cases; compare key values and update boundaries only. A distinction establishes feasibility, not gain; absent such a distinction, stop direct transfer.
